'''Michel Boudart''' (18 June 1924 – 2 May 2012) was the William M. Keck Sr. [[Professor]] of [[Chemical engineering]] Emeritus at [[Stanford University]].

He earned his [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] and [[Master of Science|MS]] degrees from the [[Catholic University of Leuven (1834–1968)|University of Louvain]] in 1944 and 1947, respectively, and earned his PhD in [[chemistry]] from [[Princeton University]] in 1950 under the guidance of [[Hugh Stott Taylor]].<ref>{{cite web
|title=Chemistry Tree
|url=http://academictree.org/chemistry/tree.php?pid=57282
|publisher=Academic Tree
|accessdate=12 January 2013
}}</ref>

He was a professor at Princeton until 1961 and later spent a brief period at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he helped establish a program in catalysis and reaction engineering.

Boudart joined [[Stanford University]] in 1964, where he was best known for his contributions to [[catalysis]] and for his role in the development of chemical engineering at Stanford.<ref>{{cite news
|last=Myers
|first=Andrew
|title=MICHEL BOUDART, CHEMICAL ENGINEER AND EXPERT IN CATALYSIS, DIES AT 87
|url=https://engineering.stanford.edu/obituary/michel-boudart-chemical-engineer-and-expert-catalysis-dies-87
|accessdate=12 January 2013
|newspaper=Stanford Engineering
|date=7 May 2012
}}</ref>

In 1994, he became a professor emeritus. He was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Engineering]] and a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], and the [[California Academy of Sciences]].

==Personal life==
Born in Brussels, during the Second World War, he was accepted to the University of Louvain but the university was closed. He was married to his wife Marina d'Haese Boudart. They were avid world travelers and had a daughter and three sons.<ref name="Stanford Report">{{cite news|last=Myers|first=Andrew|title=Michel Boudart, Stanford chemical engineer and expert in catalysis, dies at 87|url=http://news.stanford.edu/news/2012/may/michel-boudart-obit-050912.html|accessdate=12 January 2013|newspaper=Stanford Report|date=May 9, 2012}}</ref>
